entry.label: Systemic governance
entry.description: Systemic governance treats governing as the design and continuing adaptation of relationships, institutions, learning processes and accountabilities across interacting systems rather than as command from one centre.
entry.canonical_definition: Systemic governance treats governing as the design and continuing adaptation of relationships, institutions, learning processes and accountabilities across interacting systems rather than as command from one centre.

profile.title: Systemic governance
profile.canonical_definition: Systemic governance treats governing as the design and continuing adaptation of relationships, institutions, learning processes and accountabilities across interacting systems rather than as command from one centre.
profile.summary: Systemic governance concerns the institutions, relations and learning processes through which multiple actors govern together across boundaries and levels.
profile.why_it_matters: Complex public issues exceed the variety and authority of any single organisation. Governance has to distribute sensing, action and accountability while preserving the capacity to learn and adapt.
key_distinctions: distributed agency vs absence of accountability
open_checks: distinguish democratic legitimacy from functional viability
profile.editorial_note: Developed from public primary, institutional and publisher sources. Open to correction, rival interpretation and stronger evidence.
